boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all ten frozen records in the Gettysburg Campaign [June-July 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates. Middleburg (June 17–19) overlaps Aldie (June 17), and Boonsboro (July 8) lies inside Williamsport's frozen interval (July 6–16); campaign-wide and multi-day totals (for example Stuart's June 17–21 losses and the Count of Paris's campaign estimates) must not be assigned to one engagement or added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions and the live field zero. NPS says Duffié's isolated 1st Rhode Island Cavalry was attacked on June 17 by Munford's and Robertson's brigades; Doubleday calls Duffié's command a division and says Stuart concentrated his forces against it. On June 19 NPS says J. Irvin Gregg's brigade advanced.
claims.rationale: The Union force on June 17 is a regiment in NPS and a division in Doubleday; no count is given. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. NPS says the 1st Rhode Island was routed on June 17, and that on June 19 Gregg drove Stuart a mile beyond the town before Stuart fell back to a second ridge still covering the Blue Ridge approaches. Doubleday says Duffié was driven out and fought his way back to Centreville.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 390 total; the live field reads zero. NPS says the 1st Rhode Island took about 250 casualties; Stuart says Robertson took 70 prisoners and a standard.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Stuart's loss of 65 killed, 279 wounded and 166 missing covers Aldie, Middleburg and Upperville together (June 17–21) and is not assigned to one engagement. The regiment's 250 is one part of the frozen interval.

open_questions: Duffié's, Gregg's, Robertson's and Chambliss's reports and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded the First Corps at Gettysburg) and Humphreys an interested history by Meade's later chief of staff; both drew on official papers. Lee's and Stuart's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXVII, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
